name: Windows Subsystem for Linux
summary: Run Linux command line tools inside Windows.
what: Turns on the Windows Subsystem for Linux and the Virtual Machine Platform it needs for version 2.
benefit: Use Linux shells, package managers and developer tools without a separate virtual machine.
risk: Low. Needs a restart. Hardware virtualization must be enabled in the firmware.
advice: Suggested for developers and anyone who needs Linux tools. Skip it if you do not.
facts: WSL 2 also needs the Virtual Machine Platform, so both are turned on
Works on Home and Pro
Restart required
A Linux distribution is installed separately afterward

name: Hyper-V virtual machines
summary: Run virtual machines with the built in hypervisor.
what: Turns on all Hyper-V components, including the hypervisor, management tools and services.
benefit: Create and run virtual machines with no extra software.
risk: Low. Windows then runs on top of the hypervisor, which a few older emulators and some anti-cheat or VR tools do not support.
advice: Suggested if you run virtual machines. Skip it if you play games with strict anti-cheat or use older emulators.
facts: Not available on Home
Needs hardware virtualization with second level address translation
Windows runs on top of the hypervisor once it is on
Restart required

name: Windows Sandbox
summary: A throwaway Windows desktop for testing unknown files.
what: Turns on the disposable desktop environment. Everything inside is erased when the window closes.
benefit: Open a suspicious download or try an installer without risking your real system.
risk: Low. Needs a restart and virtualization support.
advice: Suggested if you try unknown programs. Safe to skip otherwise.
facts: Not available on Home
Everything inside is deleted when you close it
Needs hardware virtualization enabled
Restart required

name: .NET Framework 3.5
summary: Support for older programs built on .NET 2.0 to 3.5.
what: Turns on .NET Framework 3.5, which includes 2.0 and 3.0.
benefit: Lets older apps and installers that ask for .NET 3.5 run.
risk: Low. Windows may need to download files through Windows Update, so an internet connection is needed.
advice: Suggested only if an app asks for .NET 3.5. Otherwise leave it off.
facts: Newer .NET versions do not replace it for apps built on 2.0 to 3.5
Files are downloaded from Windows Update when needed
Turning it off removes it again

name: Legacy game components
summary: Support for very old games that use DirectPlay.
what: Turns on Legacy Components and DirectPlay.
benefit: Lets a small number of games from the late 1990s and 2000s start and use their networking.
advice: Suggested only if an old game asks for DirectPlay. Otherwise leave it off.
facts: DirectPlay is an old game networking library
Only a few old titles need it
Turning it off removes it again

name: NFS client
summary: Connect to Network File System shares from Linux and NAS devices.
what: Turns on the client side of Services for NFS.
benefit: Mount shares from NFS servers as drives.
advice: Suggested only if you use NFS shares.
facts: Client only, it does not share your files
Not available on Home
Turning it off removes it again

name: OpenSSH server
summary: Let other computers sign in to this PC over SSH.
what: Installs the OpenSSH server component. It does not start the service for you.
benefit: Remote command line access and file copy over an encrypted connection.
risk: Medium. Once started it is a remote sign in service. Use key based sign in and a firewall.
advice: Suggested only if you need remote access to this PC. Skip it otherwise.
facts: Installs the component only and you choose when to start the sshd service
A running SSH server is reachable from the network
Turning it off removes the component

name: Turn off SMB 1.0
summary: Disable the old, insecure file sharing protocol.
what: Turns off the SMB 1.0 client and server features.
benefit: Closes a protocol the vendor tells everyone to stop using.
risk: Low. Very old network drives and printers that only speak SMB 1.0 stop connecting.
advice: Suggested for everyone. Skip it only if an old device on your network needs it.
facts: SMB 1.0 is deprecated by the vendor
Recent Windows versions already ship with it off
Only very old NAS devices and printers still need it
Restart may be needed
